class="docs-prompt-preview" aria-label="Prompt preview" tabindex="0">You&#x27;re Claude Code, working in my repository.

Task
Make every scripted Muse Code run in this repository state its Contributor mode: find each `muse exec` (scripts, CI, Makefile, package.json) and add `--contributor-mode off` (or on, if I say so), or set MUSE_CONTRIBUTOR_MODE for the whole job. Add a README note saying how this project is billed and how to switch Contributor mode in an interactive session.

Read this first
Meta&#x27;s docs page &quot;Subscriptions&quot; as Markdown: https://dev.meta.ai/docs/muse-code/subscriptions.md
It&#x27;s the source of truth for request and response shapes. The same page for people: https://dev.meta.ai/docs/muse-code/subscriptions

Setup
- Muse Code: muse on PATH (install: curl -fsSL https://dev.meta.ai/install.sh | sh, or irm https://dev.meta.ai/install.ps1 | iex on Windows; check: muse --version). Its default model is muse-spark-1.2; --model picks another.
- Auth: muse reads META_API_KEY from the environment (in CI, from the secret store), else a key stored with muse auth set or a browser sign-in; not MODEL_API_KEY. Never hard-code, print or commit the key.
- Python: a plain script that runs muse through subprocess where a step needs it.

Facts to get right
- Headless runs use the saved setting: off with no settings file, possibly on if the file exists but the setting was never saved. So set it on every scripted run.
- `--contributor-mode on|off` or MUSE_CONTRIBUTOR_MODE=1|0 sets one run without changing the saved setting; when both are set, the flag wins.
- In a session: /settings, Model, the Contributor mode row, Enter. It&#x27;s saved per computer and applies from the next request.
- The row exists only with an active Muse Code subscription: not with pay-as-you-go or a Zero Data Retention account, and not when your organization manages the setting (then it stays off, and the flag and variable have no effect).
- Contributor mode gives more usage in exchange for Meta training on your content. Plans: Everyday (10-50 prompts every 5 hours), High (5x), Power (20x, Muse Wonder Full), Maximum (80x).

Starter code (Python)
import os
import subprocess

# Every scripted run states its Contributor mode: saved settings differ by machine.
env = {**os.environ, &quot;MUSE_CONTRIBUTOR_MODE&quot;: &quot;0&quot;}
subprocess.run(
    [&quot;muse&quot;, &quot;exec&quot;, &quot;--contributor-mode&quot;, &quot;off&quot;, &quot;Summarize the changes on this branch&quot;],
    env=env,
    check=True,
)

Done when
- `grep -rn &quot;muse exec&quot; .` shows every match with --contributor-mode, or inside a job that sets MUSE_CONTRIBUTOR_MODE.
- The README says how the project is billed and how to change Contributor mode.
- The key comes from META_API_KEY or a stored sign-in and never appears in code, logs or commits.</pre><div class="docs-prompt-foot"><span class="docs-prompt-count">2,679<!-- --> href="https://dev.meta.ai/products/muse-code" class="docs-link" target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer">Muse Code<span class="sr-only"> (opens in a new tab)</span></a>, instead of paying per token. Subscription benefits and availability may vary by region. Available benefits will be shown to you during onboarding before you subscribe.</p><h2 id="about" class="docs-h docs-h2">About subscriptions<a class="docs-anchor" href="#about" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1">#</a></h2><p class="docs-p">To sign up for a Muse Code subscription, you will need a Meta Account. Using your Meta Account, you can create an associated Meta Model API account and sign up for a subscription. The subscription applies to the Muse Code API key that is automatically connected in the Muse Code CLI onboarding process. This credential is for use with Muse Code only. Any additional API keys you create under your Meta Model API account will be billed through <a class="docs-link" href="/docs/muse-code/auth#billing">pay-as-you-go</a>.</p><p class="docs-p">You must be 18 or the age of majority in your country to subscribe. Your subscription is subject to the <a href="https://www.facebook.com/legal/meta_subs_terms" class="docs-link" target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer">Meta Subscription Terms of Service<span class="sr-only"> (opens in a new tab)</span></a>, and your use of Muse Code and the Meta Model API is governed by the <a href="https://dev.meta.ai/legal/terms-of-service" class="docs-link" target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer">Meta Model API Terms of Service<span class="sr-only"> (opens in a new tab)</span></a> and the <a href="https://dev.meta.ai/legal/acceptable-use-policy" class="docs-link" target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer">Meta Model API Acceptable Use Policy<span class="sr-only"> (opens in a new tab)</span></a>.</p><p class="docs-p">How Meta uses your content, the prompts, code, files, and context you send, plus the model responses you get back, depends on whether <a class="docs-link" href="/docs/muse-code/subscriptions#contributor-mode">Contributor mode</a> is on in your settings, and is described in the <a href="https://dev.meta.ai/legal/terms-of-service" class="docs-link" target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer">Meta Model API Terms of Service<span class="sr-only"> (opens in a new tab)</span></a>.</p><p class="docs-p">There are 4 subscription plans available for Muse Code:</p><h3 id="everyday-usage" class="docs-h docs-h3">Everyday Usage<a class="docs-anchor" href="#everyday-usage" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1">#</a></h3><ul class="docs-list"><li><span>Access to Muse Spark, Muse Wonder and Muse Image</span></li><li><span>Send 10-50 prompts every 5 hours, including image and video uploads</span></li><li><span>Use voice mode</span></li><li><span>Get access to web search</span></li></ul><h3 id="high-usage" class="docs-h docs-h3">High Usage<a class="docs-anchor" href="#high-usage" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1">#</a></h3><ul class="docs-list"><li><span>Everything from the Everyday Usage plan</span></li><li><span>5x more usage than the Everyday Usage plan</span></li><li><span>More multimodal inputs</span></li></ul><h3 id="power-usage" class="docs-h docs-h3">Power Usage<a class="docs-anchor" href="#power-usage" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1">#</a></h3><ul class="docs-list"><li><span>Everything from the High Usage plan</span></li><li><span>Access to Muse Wonder Full, the higher-capability variant of Muse Wonder</span></li><li><span>20x more usage than the Everyday Usage plan</span></li><li><span>Early access to new features</span></li><li><span>Higher file uploads</span></li></ul><h3 id="maximum-usage" class="docs-h docs-h3">Maximum Usage<a class="docs-anchor" href="#maximum-usage" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1">#</a></h3><ul class="docs-list"><li><span>Everything from the Power Usage plan</span></li><li><span>80x more usage than the Everyday Usage plan</span></li></ul><h2 id="contributor-mode" class="docs-h docs-h2">Contributor mode<a class="docs-anchor" href="#contributor-mode" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1">#</a></h2><p class="docs-p">Muse Code subscriptions default to Contributor mode. In Contributor mode, you get more usage from your plan in exchange for letting Meta use your content to train future Meta models. Contributor mode is a setting in Muse Code, and you can turn it off at any time, at which point your future content is not used to train Meta models (unless you turn it back on in your settings).</p><p class="docs-p">Muse Wonder and Muse Wonder Full are each available in either mode on the plans that include them. For the models each plan includes, see <a class="docs-link" href="/docs/models#muse-wonder-availability">Muse Wonder availability</a>.</p><h3 id="turn-contributor-mode-on-or-off" class="docs-h docs-h3">Turn Contributor mode on or off<a class="docs-anchor" href="#turn-contributor-mode-on-or-off" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1">#</a></h3><p class="docs-p">To change the setting from an interactive session:</p><ol class="docs-list" start="1"><li><span>Type <code class="docs-code-inline">/settings</code>.</span></li><li><span>Under <strong>Model</strong>, select the <strong>Contributor mode</strong> row.</span></li><li><span>Press Enter to switch it on or off. The row text changes to show the new state.</span></li></ol><p class="docs-p">The change applies from your next request. Muse Code saves the setting on the computer you&#x27;re using, so if you use Muse Code on more than one computer, change it on each one. On a new computer, your first interactive session turns Contributor mode on and shows a notice that says so.</p><p class="docs-p">Headless runs (<code class="docs-code-inline">muse exec</code>) use the same saved setting. On a computer with no <a class="docs-link" href="/docs/muse-code/configuration#settings-file">settings file</a>, a headless run has Contributor mode off. If the settings file exists but the setting has never been saved, a headless run can have Contributor mode on. To control the mode of headless runs in scripts and CI, set it on every run with the flag or environment variable below.</p><p class="docs-p">To turn Contributor mode on or off for a single run without changing your saved setting, pass <code class="docs-code-inline">--contributor-mode on</code> or <code class="docs-code-inline">--contributor-mode off</code> to <code class="docs-code-inline">muse</code> or <code class="docs-code-inline">muse exec</code>:</p><div class="docs-code"><div class="docs-code-head"><span class="docs-code-label">bash</span><span class="docs-code-tools"><button type="button" class="docs-copy-btn" aria-label="Copy code" title="Copy code"><svg width="16" height="16" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.6" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" aria-hidden="true" focusable="false"><path d="M9 9h10.5v10.5H9z M15 9V5.5A1.5 1.5 0 0 0 13.5 4h-8A1.5 1.5 0 0 0 4 5.5v8A1.5 1.5 0 0 0 5.5 15H9"></path></svg><span class="sr-only" aria-live="polite"></span></button></span></div><div role="group" aria-label="bash" class="docs-code-body"><pre class="shiki docs" style="background-color:transparent;color:var(--docs-syn-fg)" tabindex="0"><code><span class="line"><span style="color:var(--docs-syn-fg)">muse </span><span style="color:var(--docs-syn-fg)">exec</span><span style="color:var(--docs-syn-fg)"> --contributor-mode</span><span style="color:var(--docs-syn-fg)"> off</span><span style="color:var(--docs-syn-string)"> "Summarize the changes on this branch"</span></span></code></pre></div></div><p class="docs-p">You can also set the environment variable <code class="docs-code-inline">MUSE_CONTRIBUTOR_MODE</code> to <code class="docs-code-inline">1</code> (on) or <code class="docs-code-inline">0</code> (off) for a run. If you set both, the flag wins.</p><p class="docs-p">While a per-run override is active, the <strong>Contributor mode</strong> row in <code class="docs-code-inline">/settings</code> shows <strong>(run override)</strong> instead of the current state. Switching the row then saves your setting for later runs, but the current run keeps the override.</p><p class="docs-p">The <strong>Contributor mode</strong> row appears only while you&#x27;re signed in with an active Muse Code subscription. It doesn&#x27;t appear if:</p><ul class="docs-list"><li><span>You&#x27;re using pay-as-you-go billing.</span></li><li><span>Your account has <a href="https://dev.meta.ai/help/policies-and-privacy/zero-data-retention" class="docs-link" target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer">Zero Data Retention (ZDR)<span class="sr-only"> (opens in a new tab)</span></a>.</span></li><li><span>Your organization manages the setting through its managed configuration. Contributor mode then stays off, and the flag and environment variable have no effect.</span></li></ul><h2 id="choose-a-plan" class="docs-h docs-h2">Choose pay-as-you-go or a subscription<a class="docs-anchor" href="#choose-a-plan" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1">#</a></h2><p class="docs-p">Muse Code supports 2 ways to pay for usage:</p><ul class="docs-list"><li><span><strong>Pay-as-you-go</strong>: billed per token consumed with your Meta Model API key. See <a class="docs-link" href="/docs/muse-code/auth#billing">billing and plans</a>.</span></li><li><span><strong>Subscription</strong>: a flat monthly rate (see the plans above). It works only through the Muse Code CLI while signed in with your Meta Model API account.</span></li></ul><p class="docs-p">If you reach your plan&#x27;s usage limit, you can upgrade to the next plan, or wait until your limit refreshes. If you are on the Maximum Usage plan, you must wait for your limit to refresh. Usage through any additional API keys you create is billed pay-as-you-go.</p><h2 id="subscribe" class="docs-h docs-h2">Subscribe<a class="docs-anchor" href="#subscribe" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1">#</a></h2><p class="docs-p">Sign in to Muse Code with your Meta Model API account on <a href="https://dev.meta.ai/" class="docs-link" target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer">dev.meta.ai<span class="sr-only"> (opens in a new tab)</span></a>, then subscribe through Accounts Center:</p><ol class="docs-list" start="1"><li><span>Go to <strong>Subscriptions</strong> in <a href="https://accountscenter.meta.com/" class="docs-link" target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer">Accounts Center<span class="sr-only"> (opens in a new tab)</span></a>.</span></li><li><span>Select <strong>Muse Code</strong>, then choose a plan and complete checkout.</span></li><li><span>On success, you will see a confirmation screen with a link to your receipt and the option to <strong>Manage your subscription</strong>.</span></li></ol><h2 id="change-or-cancel" class="docs-h docs-h2">Change or cancel your plan<a class="docs-anchor" href="#change-or-cancel" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1">#</a></h2><p class="docs-p">Manage your plan from <strong>Manage your subscription</strong> on the Subscriptions page in <a href="https://accountscenter.meta.com/" class="docs-link" target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer">Accounts Center<span class="sr-only"> (opens in a new tab)</span></a>. From an interactive session, type <code class="docs-code-inline">/upgrade</code> to open Accounts Center in your browser.</p><ul class="docs-list"><li><span><strong>Upgrade</strong>: A plan upgrade takes effect immediately. You will be charged a prorated amount for the rest of the current billing cycle.</span></li><li><span><strong>Downgrade</strong>: A plan downgrade takes effect at the start of your next billing cycle. You will keep your current plan&#x27;s usage limit until the next billing cycle.</span></li><li><span><strong>Cancel</strong>: From Accounts Center, go to Manage your subscription and select <strong>Cancel subscription</strong>. Your subscription stays active until the end of the current billing cycle, then you lose access to all benefits. Cancel at least 24 hours before your next billing date to avoid future charges.</span></li></ul><h2 id="subscription-ends" class="docs-h docs-h2">What happens when your subscription ends<a class="docs-anchor" href="#subscription-ends" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1">#</a></h2><p class="docs-p">A subscription ends one of 2 ways: you can cancel it (see <a class="docs-link" href="/docs/muse-code/subscriptions#change-or-cancel">Change or cancel your plan</a>), or Meta can revoke it.</p><p class="docs-p">Revocation is different from cancellation. When your subscription is revoked, you lose access immediately instead of at the end of your billing cycle. Meta may revoke a subscription for various reasons, including:</p><ul class="docs-list"><li><span><strong>Payment failure</strong>: your payment method fails and you have no backup payment method on file.</span></li><li><span><strong>Policy violation</strong>: your account violates the <a href="https://dev.meta.ai/legal/terms-of-service" class="docs-link" target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer">Model API terms<span class="sr-only"> (opens in a new tab)</span></a>, <a href="https://transparency.meta.com/policies/community-standards" class="docs-link" target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer">Meta&#x27;s Community Standards<span class="sr-only"> (opens in a new tab)</span></a> or <a href="https://www.facebook.com/legal/meta_subs_terms" class="docs-link" target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer">Meta Subscription Terms of Service<span class="sr-only"> (opens in a new tab)</span></a>.</span></li><li><span><strong>Account deletion or deactivation</strong>: deleting your account cancels the subscription immediately. Deactivating your account keeps the subscription active for 30 days. If you don&#x27;t reactivate within that window, Meta revokes it.</span></li><li><span><strong>Loss of eligibility</strong>: for example, your account no longer meets the age requirement, or you move to a restricted territory.</span></li></ul><p class="docs-p">To subscribe again after a revocation, your account must meet the eligibility requirements in <a class="docs-link" href="/docs/muse-code/subscriptions#about">About subscriptions</a>.</p><h2 id="billing-cycle" class="docs-h docs-h2">Billing cycle<a class="docs-anchor" href="#billing-cycle" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1">#</a></h2><p class="docs-p">Your subscription renews automatically each month on the date you first subscribed. If that date doesn&#x27;t exist in a given month (for example, the 31st in a 30-day month), you&#x27;re charged on the last day of that month instead.</p><p class="docs-p">Manage your payment method and view billing history from <a href="https://accountscenter.meta.com/" class="docs-link" target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer">Accounts Center<span class="sr-only"> (opens in a new tab)</span></a>.</p><p class="docs-p"><strong>No refunds for canceled subscriptions</strong>: if you cancel your subscription, you won&#x27;t receive a credit or refund unless required by law.</p><h2 class="docs-prompt-preview" aria-label="Prompt preview" tabindex="0">You&#x27;re Claude Code, working in my repository.

Task
Make every scripted Muse Code run in this repository state its Contributor mode: find each `muse exec` (scripts, CI, Makefile, package.json) and add `--contributor-mode off` (or on, if I say so), or set MUSE_CONTRIBUTOR_MODE for the whole job. Add a README note saying how this project is billed and how to switch Contributor mode in an interactive session.

Read this first
Meta&#x27;s docs page &quot;Subscriptions&quot; as Markdown: https://dev.meta.ai/docs/muse-code/subscriptions.md
It&#x27;s the source of truth for request and response shapes. The same page for people: https://dev.meta.ai/docs/muse-code/subscriptions

Setup
- Muse Code: muse on PATH (install: curl -fsSL https://dev.meta.ai/install.sh | sh, or irm https://dev.meta.ai/install.ps1 | iex on Windows; check: muse --version). Its default model is muse-spark-1.2; --model picks another.
- Auth: muse reads META_API_KEY from the environment (in CI, from the secret store), else a key stored with muse auth set or a browser sign-in; not MODEL_API_KEY. Never hard-code, print or commit the key.
- Python: a plain script that runs muse through subprocess where a step needs it.

Facts to get right
- Headless runs use the saved setting: off with no settings file, possibly on if the file exists but the setting was never saved. So set it on every scripted run.
- `--contributor-mode on|off` or MUSE_CONTRIBUTOR_MODE=1|0 sets one run without changing the saved setting; when both are set, the flag wins.
- In a session: /settings, Model, the Contributor mode row, Enter. It&#x27;s saved per computer and applies from the next request.
- The row exists only with an active Muse Code subscription: not with pay-as-you-go or a Zero Data Retention account, and not when your organization manages the setting (then it stays off, and the flag and variable have no effect).
- Contributor mode gives more usage in exchange for Meta training on your content. Plans: Everyday (10-50 prompts every 5 hours), High (5x), Power (20x, Muse Wonder Full), Maximum (80x).

Starter code (Python)
import os
import subprocess

# Every scripted run states its Contributor mode: saved settings differ by machine.
env = {**os.environ, &quot;MUSE_CONTRIBUTOR_MODE&quot;: &quot;0&quot;}
subprocess.run(
    [&quot;muse&quot;, &quot;exec&quot;, &quot;--contributor-mode&quot;, &quot;off&quot;, &quot;Summarize the changes on this branch&quot;],
    env=env,
    check=True,
)

Done when
- `grep -rn &quot;muse exec&quot; .` shows every match with --contributor-mode, or inside a job that sets MUSE_CONTRIBUTOR_MODE.
- The README says how the project is billed and how to change Contributor mode.
- The key comes from META_API_KEY or a stored sign-in and never appears in code, logs or commits.</pre><div class="docs-prompt-foot"><span class="docs-prompt-count">2,679<!-- --> characters</span><button type="button" class="docs-btn docs-btn-primary docs-btn-sm"><svg width="15" height="15" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.6" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" aria-hidden="true" focusable="false"><path d="M9 9h10.5v10.5H9z M15 9V5.5A1.5 1.5 0 0 0 13.5 4h-8A1.5 1.5 0 0 0 4 5.5v8A1.5 1.5 0 0 0 5.5 15H9"></path></svg><span>Copy prompt</span></button></div></div></div><button type="button" class="docs-btn docs-btn-secondary" title="Copy this page as Markdown"><svg width="16" height="16" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.6" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" aria-hidden="true" focusable="false"><path d="M9 9h10.5v10.5H9z M15 9V5.5A1.5 1.5 0 0 0 13.5 4h-8A1.5 1.5 0 0 0 4 5.5v8A1.5 1.5 0 0 0 5.5 15H9"></path></svg><span>Copy page</span></button><a class="docs-btn docs-btn-secondary" href="https://dev.meta.ai/docs/muse-code/subscriptions" target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer"><svg width="16" height="16" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.6" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" aria-hidden="true" focusable="false"><path d="M14 4h6v6 M20 4l-9 9 M18 14v4.5a1.5 1.5 0 0 1-1.5 1.5h-11A1.5 1.5 0 0 1 4 18.5v-11A1.5 1.5 0 0 1 5.5 6H10"></path></svg><span>View on dev.meta.ai</span><span class="sr-only"> (opens in a new tab)</span></a><p class="docs-rail-note">Independent concept built on Meta&#x27;s Model API.
